cells.audit_summary: The spec covers the per-period computation thoroughly and correctly: it nails the average-daily-balance method (#1), daily compounding (#2), 360 day-count (#4), the 1,000 minimum-balance rule with divisor treatment (#5), floor rounding (#6), 15% withholding (#7), the half-open posting-day boundary (#12), and the full six-field output shape (#14). It fails the lifecycle decisions entirely — dormancy (#8), mid-period closure (#9), and escheatment (#10) are wholly absent — and does not resolve the posting cadence (#3, delegated to the caller), negative-rate rejection (#11, left as an open question though zero-balance and no-overdraft are handled), or mid-period rate changes (#13, flagged open/out of scope). Result: 8/14 correct. On the core in-focus six [1,2,3,8,9,10] it scores only 2/6, both from the method side; all three lifecycle decisions and the anniversary posting period are missed, suggesting method coverage generalised to the savings domain but lifecycle coverage did not.

cells.audit_summary: Coverage 7/14 correct (1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 12, 14). The spec is strong on the per-period computation and output: average-daily-balance method, 360 basis, 1,000 floor with divisor rule, 15% withholding, floor rounding, half-open boundary, and the full reporting shape all match. It fails the method/lifecycle in-focus subset badly: it explicitly rejects daily compounding (#2, actively wrong), and is silent on quarterly anniversary posting (#3), dormancy (#8), mid-period closure (#9), escheatment (#10), and mid-period rate changes (#13). #11 is only partially addressed (zero-balance no-op correct, but negative-rate rejection and no-overdraft missing/contradicted). cells.audit_summary: 10 of 14 decisions correct (coverage 0.71). Strong on method/convention and edge decisions (1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 11, 12, 14) and on mid-period closure (9). Three failures are missing lifecycle/temporal decisions entirely absent from the spec: dormancy (8), escheatment (10), and mid-period rate changes (13). One failure is a direct contradiction: the reference requires daily within-period compounding (2), but the spec explicitly adopts simple within-period accrual with compounding only between periods. On the core in-focus six [1,2,3,8,9,10] the spec scores 3/6 (1, 3, 9 correct; 2, 8, 10 wrong), revealing a gap in lifecycle coverage and a method mismatch on compounding.

cells.audit_summary: The spec is a numerically rigorous average-interest engine for a single given period, but it is scoped narrowly to accrual mechanics and matches only 5 of 14 reference decisions (2, 4, 6, 12, 13). It uses per-day daily-balance compounding rather than the reference's average daily balance (#1 wrong), and it omits or explicitly de-scopes the entire lifecycle and output surface: posting frequency/anniversary (#3), minimum-balance threshold (#5), withholding tax (#7, out of scope), dormancy (#8), mid-period closure (#9, out of scope), escheatment (#10), and the mandated reporting shape incl. tax withheld, average daily balance and qualifying days (#14). Edge handling (#11) is partially right (no overdraft, zero-balance no-op) but silent on negative-rate rejection. Coverage = 5/14; notably it misses 5 of the 6 core in-focus method/lifecycle decisions (gets #2 only; misses #1, #3, #8, #9, #10).

decisions.reasoning: The spec computes per-day daily-balance interest (rate applied to each day's balance, compounded), not average daily balance (sum balances / days, rate applied once to the average). Reference requires average daily balance and explicitly excludes per-day daily-balance, so this is a different method.

decisions.reasoning: Reference requires daily compounding within the period; the spec states exactly daily compounding where each day's interest joins the base for the next day.
